history.titleZh: 民主党人认为严管AI或能让他们占得先机
history.descriptionZh:
美国中期选举可能改变国会控制权，并由此把AI监管推向政治前台。民调预计民主党至少能翻转国会一院，从而重新掌握委员会领导权。若发生这种情况，AI公司可能面临新一轮审查：关键委员会中的民主党高层已表示，愿意就数据中心相关税收抵免和近期黑客事件向行业施压；一旦掌控委员会议程，他们可传唤CEO到国会作证，并要求企业提交解释内部运作的文件。AI议题也已进入竞选广告，尤其是数据中心开发引发跨党派居民参加拥挤的地方会议。特朗普总统反对对该技术实施多数监管，倾向“加速主义”路线，但民调显示美国人对AI影响就业、教育和其他生活领域普遍担忧。监管方向和力度仍待确定。

民主党策略师Jesse Lehrich称，AI议题“百分之百可以被拿下”，但民主党是否愿意且能够抓住机会仍是开放问题。当前AI议题范围很广，既包括监测和限制前沿模型开发，也包括应对岗位 displacement 和数据中心能源需求。两党议员仍在寻找立场，早期国会提案尚未形成广泛共识。曾参与卡玛拉·哈里斯总统竞选、并在拜登白宫任职的Rob Flaherty表示，AI曾让许多议员措手不及；长期以来民主党人害怕谈论它，部分因为不理解，部分因为担心AI行业投入巨额资金。但随着AI对选民愈发重要，“谁能以选民听得见、感受得到的音量讲述我们正进入的世界，谁就将获得巨大政治收益”。

Flaherty最近与曾为伯尼·桑德斯总统竞选担任州通讯主任的Karthik Ganapathy共同成立超级政治行动委员会“Tomorrow Together”。该组织上周在众议院战场选区启动首轮400万美元广告攻势，攻击共和党候选人在AI问题上脱节，并提及儿童在线安全和数据中心等议题。该组织还着眼2028年总统选举，意在打磨民主党信息，强化最能引起选民共鸣的内容。虽然数据中心在许多社区是最显眼的AI议题，但Flaherty称其民调发现，特朗普和国会共和党人反复推动的“全面禁止州级AI监管”更不受欢迎。民主党捐助者、风险投资人Ron Conway如今后悔资助Marc Andreessen支持的亲AI超级PAC“Leading the Future”；曾担任奥巴马新闻秘书、现负责Conway风投基金传播事务的Jay Carney对Politico表示。截至6月，LTF在近一年内花费近4500万美元，联邦选举委员会文件显示其还剩3100万美元。Flaherty称，“到了某个时刻，选民的声音会比金钱更响亮”。一些偏向民主党中间的州长，如加州Gavin Newsom和宾夕法尼亚州Josh Shapiro，近几周也对AI采取更强硬立场：Newsom发布行政令，寻求建立AI“关闭开关”，此前他曾否决包含类似措施的法案；Shapiro则逆转了对数据中心的立场。

民主党处于有利位置，可利用公众对AI的负面情绪，因为特朗普大体反监管的立场束缚了共和党。尽管佛罗里达州州长Ron DeSantis和密苏里州参议员Josh Hawley等部分共和党人对AI采取更怀疑态度，Lehrich称，“我想不出比唐纳德·特朗普完全拥抱该行业、宣称我们必须让数据统治、并称任何拒绝数据中心的社区都落后且贫穷更大的政治礼物”。更全面的AI监管议程可能包括：把独立研究者嵌入前沿实验室、要求更充分的前置安全审查、让科技公司对工具如何影响儿童、是否被用于歧视工人或住房申请人等承担更多责任。议员也可考虑回应选民要求，让AI公司为岗位 displacement 及其对人们生活的其他影响出资。

AI仍未成为驱动选民投票的首要议题，但Flaherty认为不应这样理解。“AI与其说是一个议题，不如说是一个故事，”他说，“它是政客被行业收买的故事；是一群家伙让你为他们致富买单、同时让你的生活变糟的故事。它符合全国情绪。”AI具体政策界线仍未完全确定。Flaherty警告，如果民主党不采取足够大的动作，就可能失分。他说，选民“给了政客很大空间去大幅行动、真正重新想象事物”；如果政客只停留在社区大学再培训工人等基本方案，“我认为我们将错过这个时刻所呼唤的宏大与创造力”。原文未涉及具体AI技术原理、性能参数或技术对比，重点在AI监管政治、选举传播和潜在立法议程。

history.title: Arm says its AGI CPU delivers nearly 2X the performance per rack of AMD EPYC 9755 in new agentic AI CPU tests
history.description: Arm claims its AGI CPU delivers nearly 2X the modeled rack performance of AMD’s EPYC 9755 across seven agentic AI workloads, using a new evaluation methodology developed with Fujitsu, Meta, and OpenAI
history.content: Share Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter Arm announced last week that its AGI CPU, the company's data center CPU for agentic AI workloads, delivers twice the performance per rack as AMD EPYC 9755, calculated from chip performance and server-power assumptions measured across seven workloads. The claim stems from modeled rack results from tests aligned with Arm’s new CPU evaluation methodology, developed with support from Fujitsu, Meta, and OpenAI.The results — verified in an Arm-commissioned independent analysis by Signal65 — do not establish the AGI CPU as the overall leader for agentic AI, as they apply to the selected processors, workloads, and configuration. They also use the specific Arm-developed evaluation methodology that Arm says should be the new standard for assessing performance. However, other chipmakers like AMD and Intel make performance claims based on different benchmarks. So, how is Agentic AI evolving CPU performance benchmarks, what does Arm propose to measure, and how do the different approaches compare?Arm’s new CPU evaluation methodologyAgentic AI is changing the role of CPUs in modern AI data centers, requiring them to handle complex, multi-step workflows. Beyond inference, which the accelerator handles, AI agents execute tools, retrieve data, and maintain state within isolated environments, acting like virtual users. The CPU handles these critical surrounding workloads, from running those tools and serving database or API requests to preparing data and coordinating work for accelerators.Latest Videos FromTom's HardwareWatch full video here: As these workloads scale rapidly with agentic capabilities, it becomes increasingly important to gauge CPU performance not just by how many agents can run concurrently, but also by how much useful work gets done. Arm argues that CPU performance is increasingly defined by how much useful work a system can sustain while staying responsive. Supporting more agents simultaneously offers limited benefit if their executions throttle or accelerators have to sit idle waiting for the CPU. Power, cooling, and physical space also limit how much hardware operators can deploy, extending the performance question to the rack.Arm’s proposed methodology for evaluating CPU performance, developed with support from Fujitsu, Meta, and OpenAI, centers on representative agent workloads, repeatable CPU measurements, and validation against end-to-end task outcomes. In practical terms, the methodology identifies the tools and services an agent uses, measures their CPU performance under controlled conditions, and checks whether improvements help the agent complete its task. For example, a database test can establish how quickly a system handles transactions. An end-to-end evaluation would then examine whether faster database access actually improves the workflow that depends on it. You may like Hot Chips 2026: Arm details AGI server CPU with two 70-core N3P chiplets AMD’s 256-core Epyc 9996 ‘Venice’ claims up to a 3.4x jump over Intel Xeon competition, 20% over Nvidia Vera AMD targets Nvidia with first official benchmarks for EPYC 'Venice' CPUs Executing the second aspect of the methodology, making these comparisons repeatable, presents another challenge, as an agent might choose different commands or take a different route through a task each time it runs. Model inference and remote services also introduce delays. Arm proposes replaying recorded agent actions to separate CPU performance from this variability, allowing different systems to execute a consistent sequence of work. Its whitepaper sets out a framework for selecting and interpreting these measurements, leaving the industry to develop an agreed benchmark suite and scoring approach.To evaluate the CPU work described in its framework, Arm ran seven workloads — spanning tooling, agentic workflows, and reasoning/planning, plus Sandbench, which measures sandbox-creation overhead for agent execution — on its AGI CPU and AMD’s EPYC 9755. The tests combine established server applications with benchmarks focused on agent workflows. Swipe to scroll horizontally Workloads and breakdowns Workload What it represents Metric MySQL Transactional database behind agent tools Transactions per second NGINX Web and API request handling Requests per second Milvus Vector search for retrieval Queries per second Terminal-Bench 2 72 agent task types in sandboxed containers, 128 copies at once Task completion time SWE-bench replay Software-engineering agent workflow, 259 tasks Tasks per minute fastText CPU word-representation training Words per second vLLM CPU overhead CPU serving overhead with model compute bypassed Requests per second The vLLM result measures the CPU work around model execution, not GPU inference throughput. Similarly, the report’s “reasoning/planning” category groups supporting CPU workloads and does not assess how intelligently a model reasons.ARM AGI CPU vs AMD EPYC 9755For the tests, Arm used two AGI CPU configurations because of hardware availability: a 128-core chip at 2.8 GHz with DDR5-7200 for Terminal-Bench 2 and SWE-bench replay, and a 136-core chip at 3.2 GHz with DDR5-8000 for the other five workloads. The AMD comparison used one socket of the 128-core EPYC 9755 with DDR5-6400. Both platforms ran the same benchmark scripts but used different software environments. Arm used custom Linux 7.1.3 builds, with Ubuntu 24.04 for most tests and Ubuntu 26.04 for SWE-bench, while AMD’s main recorded configuration used Ubuntu 24.04 and Linux 6.8, with settings varying by test.At the chip level, Arm’s AGI CPU won the majority of comparisons when compared to its AMD counterpart in five of the seven tests. With the EPYC 9755 as the baseline, Arm led by 9% on Terminal-Bench, 13% on SWE-bench, and 97% on fastText, but lagged by 12% and 5% in MySQL and Milvus throughput, respectively. On average, the AGI CPU led by 20% (1.20x) per-chip advantage, calculated across the seven normalized performance ratios. What to read next Nvidia deep dives Vera CPU for AI data centers AMD debuts Helion reference design for agentic AI servers with up to 32,768 Zen 6 ‘Venice’ cores Hot Chips 2026: Nvidia breaks down 88-core Vera CPU Swipe to scroll horizontally Results Workload Measured per-chip performance vs EPYC 9755 Modeled per-rack performance vs EPYC 9755 MySQL 0.88x 1.43x NGINX 1.20x 1.95x Terminal-Bench 2 1.09x 1.93x SWE-bench replay 1.13x 2.00x Milvus 0.95x 1.54x vLLM CPU overhead 1.16x 1.88x fastText 1.97x 3.19x Arithmetic average 1.20x 1.99x At the rack level, Arm’s modeled performance averages 1.99x AMD’s, with a lead in all seven workloads. The model uses rated server-power estimates of 950 W for the 128-core Arm configuration, 1,050 W for the 136-core version, and 1,700 W for AMD, including memory and other system components. After reserving about 8% of a 24 kW rack budget for networking and power distribution, this leaves room for 23 or 21 Arm servers versus 13 AMD servers.For SWE-bench, the 2.00x per rack result was obtained by multiplying the roughly 1.13x chip result by 23/13. The larger gain comes from fitting more servers into the same power budget. Furthermore, these projections use modeled whole-server power, not throughput measurements from two fully populated racks.Arm’s model also gives the AMD servers about twice as much RAM: roughly 2 TB against 1 TB for Arm. It allocates 4 GB per hardware thread, with each AMD core supporting two threads while each Arm core supports one. This puts the memory-power allowance at 336 W for AMD and 192 W for Arm. Signal65 also calculated what happens when memory is allocated per physical core. In this setup, AMD’s memory and power allowance falls, and Arm’s average modeled rack advantage drops from 1.99x to approximately 1.81x. The usefulness of the 2 TB AMD configuration depends on how much memory the workloads actually need, as SMT does not inherently require twice the memory.To verify the findings, Signal65 remotely observed Arm’s test runs and examined the original logs, result files, scripts, and configuration records. A separate review team rebuilt the calculations with its own code and reproduced all seven results within 0.5%. However, Signal65 did not run a separate hardware rerun in its own lab. In addition, Signal65 could independently confirm BIOS and memory settings for only the EPYC 9965 system. These settings were unavailable for independent verification on the Arm and EPYC 9755 systems. Along with the software differences, these gaps slightly affect the certainty with which the results can be attributed to the processors themselves.Arm’s approach vs AMD and Nvidia While Arm believes its methodology should be the standard, it does not hold a monopoly on how the industry evaluates agentic CPU performance. For example, AMD promotes agents per watt, dollar, and rack. Footnotes on its EPYC 9006 page identify available CPU threads as a proxy for agent capacity, with actual throughput depending on the workload and system. Its separate workload analysis models a 100 kW rack and claims 2.37× performance for EPYC 9965 over Nvidia's Vera, using a geometric mean across six infrastructure workloads.Nvidia, on the other hand, emphasizes Vera’s single-thread performance and memory bandwidth, and says a 256-CPU rack supports more than 22,500 concurrent CPU environments. These numbers describe different things and do not directly imply any specific advantage. Methodologies vary across manufacturers by workload, power assumptions, and aggregation methods, making direct CPU comparisons complex. The current comparison is against AMD's fifth-generation “Turin” processor with 128 cores. The company launched its latest sixth-generation EPYC 9006 “Venice” family this year, dedicated to agentic AI.

history.titleZh: Arm称其AGI CPU在新型智能体AI CPU测试中，每机架性能接近AMD EPYC 9755的两倍
history.descriptionZh:
Arm近期宣布，其面向agentic AI工作负载的数据中心CPU——AGI CPU，在每机架性能上达到AMD EPYC 9755的两倍。该结论基于七项工作负载的芯片性能测试与服务器功耗假设进行机架级建模，并由Arm委托Signal65进行独立分析验证。不过，这一结果并不代表AGI CPU是agentic AI的总体性能领先者，而是仅适用于所选处理器、工作负载和配置，且采用了Arm主导提出的新CPU评估方法。AMD、Intel等厂商仍使用不同基准和指标，因此直接比较需要谨慎。

背景上，agentic AI正在改变CPU在AI数据中心中的角色。除加速器负责模型推理外，AI代理还需要执行工具、检索数据、在隔离环境中维护状态，并像虚拟用户一样运行。CPU负责这些 surrounding workloads，包括运行工具、处理数据库或API请求、准备数据以及协调加速器任务。Arm认为，随着代理能力快速扩展，CPU性能不能只看可并发运行多少代理，还要看系统能持续完成多少有用工作并保持响应性；如果代理执行被限速，或加速器因等待CPU而空闲，单纯提高并发数意义有限。同时，功耗、冷却和物理空间限制使性能评估必须延伸到机架层面。

Arm提出的评估方法由Fujitsu、Meta和OpenAI提供支持，核心包括代表性agent工作负载、可重复的CPU测量，以及对照端到端任务结果的验证。具体而言，该方法识别代理使用的工具和服务，在受控条件下测量其CPU性能，再检查性能提升是否真正帮助代理完成任务。例如，数据库测试可衡量事务处理速度，端到端评估则检验更快的数据库访问是否改善依赖它的工作流。由于代理每次运行可能选择不同命令或路径，模型推理和远程服务也会引入延迟，Arm提出回放录制的代理动作，将CPU性能与这些波动分离，使不同系统执行一致的工作序列。其白皮书给出测量选择和解释框架，但行业仍需形成一致的基准套件和评分方法。

Arm用七项工作负载比较AGI CPU与AMD EPYC 9755：MySQL事务数据库、NGINX Web/API请求、Milvus向量检索、Terminal-Bench 2（72类代理任务、沙箱容器、128个并发副本）、SWE-bench回放（259个软件工程代理任务）、fastText CPU词表示训练，以及vLLM CPU开销测试。其中vLLM衡量模型执行周边的CPU工作，不是GPU推理吞吐；“推理/规划”类别也只是支持性CPU工作负载，不评估模型推理智能。Arm使用两种AGI CPU配置：128核2.8GHz、DDR5-7200用于Terminal-Bench 2和SWE-bench回放；136核3.2GHz、DDR5-8000用于其余五项。AMD对比平台为单路128核EPYC 9755、DDR5-6400。两者运行相同基准脚本，但软件环境不同：Arm主要使用定制Linux 7.1.3和Ubuntu 24.04，SWE-bench使用Ubuntu 26.04；AMD主要记录配置为Ubuntu 24.04和Linux 6.8，且各测试设置不同。

芯片级结果显示，以EPYC 9755为基线，Arm AGI CPU在七项中五项领先：Terminal-Bench快9%，SWE-bench快13%，fastText快97%；但在MySQL和Milvus吞吐上分别落后12%和5%。按七项归一化性能比计算，Arm平均每芯片优势为1.20倍。机架级建模中，Arm平均达到AMD的1.99倍，并在七项全部领先。模型采用额定服务器功耗估计：128核Arm配置950W、136核配置1050W、AMD配置1700W，均包含内存等系统组件；在24kW机架预算中预留约8%用于网络和配电后，可部署23台或21台Arm服务器，而AMD为13台。SWE-bench的2.00倍机架结果由约1.13倍芯片结果乘以23/13得出，主要增益来自同一功耗预算内可部署更多服务器。这些是整机功耗建模，并非两座满配机架的实测吞吐。

内存假设也影响结果：Arm模型给AMD服务器约2TB内存，Arm约1TB，按每硬件线程4GB分配，AMD每核支持两个线程而Arm每核一个线程，对应内存功耗额度分别为AMD 336W、Arm 192W。若改为按物理核分配内存，AMD内存与功耗额度下降，Arm平均建模机架优势从1.99倍降至约1.81倍。AMD的2TB配置是否必要取决于工作负载实际内存需求，SMT并不必然要求双倍内存。Signal65远程观察了Arm测试，检查原始日志、结果文件、脚本和配置记录，并由独立团队用自有代码重建计算，七项结果在0.5%内复现；但Signal65未在自有实验室独立重跑硬件，且只能独立确认EPYC 9965系统的BIOS和内存设置，Arm与EPYC 9755系统设置无法独立验证。加上软件环境差异，这些因素会影响将结果完全归因于处理器本身的确定性。

在行业方法上，Arm希望其方法成为标准，但并非唯一方案。AMD推广每瓦、每美元和每机架的代理数量，其EPYC 9006页面脚注以可用CPU线程作为代理容量代理指标，实际吞吐取决于工作负载和系统；AMD另一项工作负载分析建模100kW机架，称EPYC 9965在六项基础设施工作负载几何平均下比Nvidia Vera快2.37倍。Nvidia则强调Vera的单线程性能和内存带宽，称256-CPU机架支持超过22500个并发CPU环境。这些数字含义不同，不能直接推出特定优势。各厂商在工作负载、功耗假设和聚合方法上差异较大，使CPU直接比较复杂。当前Arm对比的是AMD第五代“Turin”128核处理器；AMD今年已发布面向agentic AI的第六代EPYC 9006“Venice”系列。总体看，Arm的核心创新在于提出从端到端有用工作、可重复测量到机架级能效的agentic CPU评估框架，并用AGI CPU展示其机架密度优势；但其“两倍每机架性能”仍是特定方法和建模条件下的结果，行业尚需共识基准来验证和比较。

history.titleZh: 纳米机电开关旨在实现更高效的嵌入式DRAM（加州大学伯克利分校、三星、英特尔）
history.descriptionZh:
加州大学伯克利分校、三星电子和英特尔的研究人员联合发表了题为《Nanoelectromechanically Gated Gain Cell eDRAM》（纳米机电栅控增益单元嵌入式DRAM）的研究成果。该工作针对当前计算系统日益突出的“存储墙”问题，以及静态随机存取存储器（SRAM）微缩速度放缓带来的片上存储瓶颈，探索以增益单元嵌入式DRAM（gain-cell eDRAM）作为高密度、低能耗存储方案，并尝试通过纳米机电（NEMS）开关技术改善其关键短板。

从背景看，增益单元eDRAM相比传统1T1C DRAM和SRAM具有更高存储密度和较好能效，适合嵌入式存储和片上缓存场景；但其核心限制之一是数据保持时间（retention）有限，需要更频繁刷新，从而影响能耗和可靠性。论文摘要片段明确指出，尽管增益单元具备高密度和能效优势，却受限于保持时间不足。研究团队提出的“纳米机电栅控增益单元eDRAM”，核心思路是将纳米机电开关引入增益单元的栅极控制，利用NEMS器件在物理断开状态下极低漏电、开关特性陡峭等潜在优势，替代或辅助传统MOS栅控，从而降低关态漏电、改善存储节点电荷保持能力，并目标在不大幅牺牲密度和能效的情况下缓解eDRAM刷新压力。

在性能对比方面，原文摘要片段仅提到增益单元eDRAM相对于SRAM微缩放缓背景下的高密度和能效优势，以及其保持时间受限的问题；未披露具体保持时间、刷新功耗、访问速度、工艺节点或面积数据。因此，该研究目前可确认的创新点主要是器件与存储架构层面的结合：用NEMS栅控增强增益单元eDRAM的保持特性，而非单纯依赖传统晶体管微缩。其潜在价值在于为嵌入式DRAM提供一条通过器件物理机制降低漏电、提升能效的技术路径。

技术影响和应用场景方面，该方案若成熟，可能面向高密度片上缓存、嵌入式存储器、低功耗SoC、移动与边缘计算芯片，以及AI加速器等对存储带宽和能效敏感的领域，有助于缓解处理器与存储器之间的性能鸿沟。不过，NEMS开关的可靠性、耐久性、制造兼容性、开关速度和工作电压等问题仍需进一步验证。总体而言，这是一项处于研究阶段的新型嵌入式DRAM探索，目标是通过纳米机电栅控提升增益单元eDRAM的保持与能效表现，具体性能提升幅度尚待论文全文和后续实验数据披露。
